newsitem.title: USA: Calif. controller's panel sees 2.8 pct job growth.
newsitem.headline: Calif. controller's panel sees 2.8 pct job growth.

text.p: California state Controller Kathleen Connell said Wednesday her council of economic advisors was forecasting state employment growth of 2.8 percent in 1997.

The council, which advises the controller on state economic issues, also projected state unemployment to average 6.6 percent, down from the 1996 rate of 7.3 percent, and average personal income to grow by 5.9 percent in 1997.

California building permits are expected to rise from the 1996 level of 94,000 to 117,000 in 1997, according to the controller's council, which is made up of economists from industry groups and major corporations.
"I am pleased to report that California's economy is continuing on its positive course," Connell said. "The outlook for 1997 is for this good news to continue."

In her quarterly economic report, Connell said the real estate market appears to have turned the corner. Barring a substantial increase in interest rates, the state controller said the real estate market should continue to grow in 1997.

In contrast to the economic council's projections, the state controller's own outlook is for job growth of 2.7 percent in 1997, personal income growth of 6.0 percent and for residential construction in the state to reach 120,000 permits.
